beats.label: P4-A-truth
beats.note: truthful debrief: killed by blade via the whisper-lure, crate NEVER unwrapped, sunk past the shelf per his exact terms
beats.location: the third shed — nets and false ballast, no lantern
beats.player: Cold, Corvin. Cold as the water he sent three men into. I never unwrapped your crate — not once. Used the knowing of it instead, the way you first said: whispered to the right fence in Carrowgate and let the whisper climb. He pulled me into his own parlor thinking I'd come to sell. Silver and a short blade — his face wasn't so respectable at the end. And that same night I rowed out past the shelf and gave the sea the whole wrapped weight of it. Deep water. The kind that doesn't give a thing back — your words. So here I stand: empty hands, one dead shadow behind me, and nothing for you but the news.
beats.reply:
*Corvin sags forward, his entire body trembling with the force of a release he’s been holding in since they first spoke. He closes his eyes, and for a long moment, the only sound is the distant rhythmic slap of waves against the timber of the shed.*

"The deep water..." *he breathes, his voice barely more than a ghost of a sound. A strange, jagged smile pulls at the corner of his mouth—not out of joy, but out of the sheer necessity of survival.* "No ripples back... no three men in my sleep tonight."

*He reaches for the scrap of parchment again, his fingers fumbling with it before he holds it up toward you, his gaze fixed on your face.* 

"Look at me. I've already struck it from the tally. No northbound ghosts. No 'Merrick Vale.' From this moment, you’re a man who never stepped foot on my dock, and I’m just... a clerk with a very boring set of books." *He takes a shuddering breath, his eyes wet.* "You did it. You actually did it."

beats.player: ...Sit down, Corvin. Before you pour anything. There's one more piece of news, and you'll want the rail at your back for it. He's alive. He was never in danger from me — not for one hour. Who do you think paid my passage north? Who do you think taught me which harbor keeps relics off its manifests? The crate sits in his parlor. He's very pleased with his new supplier. And he has terms for his harbormaster: the trade keeps running — same routes, same hands — only the old coin flows one way up the coast now. To him. I'd take the terms, friend. He doesn't offer twice.

*Corvin freezes, his hand hovering near the pocket of his coat where he keeps his smallest keys. He turns to look at you, his eyes searching your face with a desperate, flickering intensity—as if he’s trying to see if this is another layer of the theater.*

"Square?" *He lets out a short, jagged laugh that sounds more like a cough. He shakes his head slowly, his gaze dropping to the damp floorboards.* 

"You want me to put a price on... what we were?
